npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
npc.en: Good evening! How can I help you?
segs: I help you (to a man, after an)

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة. الْمُكَيِّف فِي الْغُرْفَة لَا يَعْمَلُ، وَالْغُرْفَة حَارَّة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Excuse me, I have a problem. The air conditioning in the room doesn't work, and the room is very hot.
choices.feedback: Good: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ ends in -ti because Salma is a woman, and حَارَّة takes ة to agree with الْغُرْفَة.

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة. الْمُكَيِّف فِي الْغُرْفَة لَا يَعْمَلُ، وَالْغُرْفَة حَارَّة جِدًّا.
choices.en: Excuse me (to a man), I have a problem. The air conditioning in the room doesn't work, and the room is very hot.
choices.feedback: سَمَحْتَ (-ta) is for a man. Salma is a woman: لَوْ سَمَحْتِ، عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة.

npc.ar: آسِفَة جِدًّا! هَلْ تُرِيدُ غُرْفَة أُخْرَى؟ عِنْدَنَا غُرْفَة أَكْبَرُ وَأَهْدَأُ فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي.
npc.en: I'm very sorry! Would you like another room? We have a bigger, quieter room on the second floor.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ أَرَاهَا أَوَّلًا؟
choices.en: Yes, please. Is it possible to see it first?
choices.feedback: Good: أَرَاهَا ends in -hā because غُرْفَة is feminine, and مِنْ فَضْلِكِ takes -ki for Salma.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. هَلْ مِنَ الْمُمْكِن أَنْ أَرَاهُ أَوَّلًا؟
choices.en: Yes, please. Is it possible to see it first? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: غُرْفَة is feminine, so 'it' is -hā: أَرَاهَا, not أَرَاهُ.

npc.ar: طَبْعًا. تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا مِفْتَاحُ الْغُرْفَة رَقْم خَمْسَة فِي الطَّابِق الثَّانِي. الْمِصْعَد عَلَى الْيَسَار.
npc.en: Of course. Here you are, this is the key to room number five on the second floor. The lift is on the left.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، وَالْمُكَيِّف يَعْمَلُ. شُكْرًا! سُؤَال آخَر: أَيْنَ نَأْكُلُ الْعَشَاء؟
choices.en: The new room is much better, and the air conditioning works. Thank you! Another question: where can we have dinner?
choices.feedback: Good: أَفْضَلُ (better) keeps one form, even with a feminine noun like الْغُرْفَة.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، شُكْرًا! وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف.
choices.en: The new room is much better, thank you! And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six.
segs: you order (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: after أَرْجُو أَنْ, the verb for a woman is تَطْلُبِي, with no final n.

choices.ar: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيد أَفْضَلُ بِكَثِير، وَالْمُكَيِّف يَعْمَلُ.
choices.en: The new room is much better, and the air conditioning works. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: الْغُرْفَة is feminine, so its adjective takes ة: الْغُرْفَة الْجَدِيدَة.

npc.ar: مَطْعَمُ الْفُنْدُق مَفْتُوح حَتَّى السَّاعَة الْعَاشِرَة، وَهُوَ أَرْخَصُ مِنْ مَطَاعِمِ الْمَدِينَة.
npc.en: The hotel restaurant is open until ten o'clock, and it's cheaper than the restaurants in town.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف إِلَى مَدْخَلِ الْبَتْرَاء.
choices.en: Excellent. And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six to the entrance of Petra.
segs: you order (to a woman, after an)
choices.feedback: Good: تَطْلُبِي is the form for a woman after أَنْ, and غَدًا carries -an as an adverb.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبَ لَنَا تَاكْسِي غَدًا فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة وَالنِّصْف إِلَى مَدْخَلِ الْبَتْرَاء.
choices.en: Excellent. And please order us a taxi tomorrow at half past six to the entrance of Petra (to a man).
segs: you order (to a man, after an)
choices.feedback: تَطْلُبَ is for a man. Salma is a woman: أَرْجُو أَنْ تَطْلُبِي لَنَا تَاكْسِي.

npc.ar: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. التَّاكْسِي يَنْتَظِرُكُمْ أَمَامَ الْفُنْدُق، وَالْفُطُور يَبْدَأُ فِي السَّاعَة السَّادِسَة.
npc.en: With pleasure. The taxi will wait for you in front of the hotel, and breakfast starts at six o'clock.
segs: it waits for you (to several people)

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر.
choices.en: Thank you very much for your help! Good night.
choices.feedback: Good: تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر is 'good night' to a woman.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر.
choices.en: Thank you very much for your help! Good night (to a man).
choices.feedback: تُصْبِحُ عَلَى خَيْر is said to a man. To Salma: تُصْبِحِينَ عَلَى خَيْر.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا يَا لَيْلَى، تَفَضَّلِي اجْلِسِي. أَنَا سَلْوَى، مُدِيرَةُ الْمَرْكَز.
npc.en: Welcome, Layla, please have a seat. I'm Salwa, the director of the centre.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. هٰذِهِ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة وَشَهَادَتِي مِنَ الْجَامِعَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much. Here are my CV and my degree certificate from the university.
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذِهِ (f) goes with سِيرَتِي, a feminine noun.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. هٰذَا سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة.
choices.en: Thank you very much. Here is my CV. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: سِيرَة is feminine, so 'this' is هٰذِهِ: هٰذِهِ سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّة.

npc.ar: قَرَأْتُ السِّيرَة الذَّاتِيَّة. أَنْتِ مِنْ لُبْنَان، وَتَدْرُسِينَ فِي الْقَاهِرَة الْآنَ، صَحِيح؟
npc.en: I've read the CV. You're from Lebanon, and you're studying in Cairo now, right?

choices.ar: صَحِيح. أَدْرُسُ فِي مَدْرَسَةِ لُغَة، وَأُسَاعِدُ زُمَلَائِي الْأَجَانِب فِي الْعَرَبِيَّة كُلَّ يَوْم.
choices.en: That's right. I study at a language school, and I help my foreign classmates with Arabic every day.
choices.feedback: Good: you confirm with صَحِيح and add what you do now, in the present tense (أَدْرُسُ، أُسَاعِدُ).

choices.ar: صَحِيح. أَنَا لُبْنَانِيّ، وَأَدْرُسُ فِي الْقَاهِرَة.
choices.en: That's right. I'm Lebanese, and I study in Cairo. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Layla is a woman, so she says لُبْنَانِيَّة, with ة: أَنَا لُبْنَانِيَّة.

npc.ar: جَمِيل. هَلْ عِنْدَكِ خِبْرَة فِي التَّعْلِيم؟
npc.en: Lovely. Do you have any experience in teaching?

choices.ar: نَعَم، فِي بَيْرُوت عَلَّمْتُ الْأَطْفَال الْعَرَبِيَّة سَنَتَيْنِ.
choices.en: Yes, in Beirut I taught Arabic to children for two years.
choices.feedback: Good: سَنَتَيْنِ (two years) tells how long, so the dual ends in -ayni.

choices.ar: نَعَم، فِي بَيْرُوت عَلَّمْتُ الْأَطْفَال الْعَرَبِيَّة سَنَتَانِ.
choices.en: Yes, in Beirut I taught Arabic to children for two years. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Here 'two years' tells how long, so the dual takes -ayni: سَنَتَيْنِ, not سَنَتَانِ.

npc.ar: مُمْتَاز. يُمْكِنُنَا أَنْ نُعْطِيَكِ صَفًّا صَغِيرًا مَسَاءَ الْأَحَد وَالثُّلَاثَاء.
npc.en: Excellent. We can give you a small class on Sunday and Tuesday evenings.
segs: we can (lit. it is possible for us)
we give you (to a woman, after an)

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَبْدَأَ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And when can I start?
segs: it is possible for me, I can
choices.feedback: Good: after يُمْكِنُنِي come أَنْ and a verb ending in -a: أَنْ أَبْدَأَ.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And what is the salary, please?
choices.feedback: Good: a polite, direct question; مِنْ فَضْلِكِ takes -ki for Mrs Salwa.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مُنَاسِب لِي. وَمَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَبْدَأُ؟
choices.en: That suits me. And when can I I start? (wrong form)
segs: it is possible for me, I can
choices.feedback: After يُمْكِنُنِي use أَنْ and a verb ending in -a: مَتَى يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَبْدَأَ؟

npc.ar: الْأُسْبُوعَ الْقَادِم، إِذَا كُنْتِ مُسْتَعِدَّة.
npc.en: Next week, if you're ready.

choices.ar: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدَّة تَمَامًا! وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I'm completely ready! And what is the salary, please?
choices.feedback: Good: a woman says مُسْتَعِدَّة, and تَمَامًا carries -an as an adverb.

choices.ar: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدّ تَمَامًا! وَمَا الرَّاتِب، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ؟
choices.en: I'm completely ready! And what is the salary, please? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: A woman says مُسْتَعِدَّة, with ة: أَنَا مُسْتَعِدَّة تَمَامًا.

npc.ar: مِئَتَا جُنَيْه لِكُلِّ دَرْس. وَسَأُرْسِلُ لَكِ الْعَقْد بِالْبَرِيدِ الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيّ الْيَوْم.
npc.en: Two hundred pounds for each lesson. And I'll send you the contract by email today.
segs: by the post, by the mail

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى! أَنَا سَعِيدَة جِدًّا بِهٰذِهِ الْوَظِيفَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, Mrs Salwa! I'm very happy with this job.
choices.feedback: Good: in an interview the title يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى keeps it formal, and سَعِيدَة agrees with Layla.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا يَا سَلْوَى! أَنَا سَعِيدَة جِدًّا بِهٰذِهِ الْوَظِيفَة.
choices.en: Thank you very much, Salwa! I'm very happy with this job.
choices.feedback: The first name alone is too familiar for the director in an interview. Use the title: يَا سَيِّدَة سَلْوَى.

npc.ar: آلُو، مَكْتَبُ كُلِّيَّةِ الْآدَاب، صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر.
npc.en: Hello, Faculty of Arts office, good morning.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. اِسْمِي فَيْصَل، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنْ مُحَاضَرَاتِ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى.
choices.en: Good morning. My name is Faisal, and I'd like to ask about Dr Mona's lectures.
choices.feedback: Good: صَبَاحُ النُّور answers صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر, and أَنْ أَسْأَلَ joins the two verbs.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَسْأَلُ عَنْ مُحَاضَرَاتِ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى.
choices.en: Good morning. I want I ask about Dr Mona's lectures. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: Join the two verbs with أَنْ, and the second one ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ.

npc.ar: تَفَضَّلْ. هَلْ أَنْتَ طَالِب فِي الْجَامِعَة؟
npc.en: Go ahead. Are you a student at the university?

choices.ar: لَا، أَنَا طَالِب فِي مَدْرَسَةِ لُغَة. هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أَحْضُرَ الْمُحَاضَرَات كُلَّ أُسْبُوع؟
choices.en: No, I'm a student at a language school. Can I attend the lectures every week?
segs: it is possible for me, I can
choices.feedback: Good: لَا answers the yes/no question, and then you say what you are instead.

choices.ar: لَا، أَنَا طَالِبَة فِي مَدْرَسَةِ لُغَة.
choices.en: No, I'm a student at a language school. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: طَالِبَة is a woman student. Faisal is a man: أَنَا طَالِب.

npc.ar: نَعَم، يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تَحْضُرَ كَضَيْف، لٰكِنْ بِدُونِ امْتِحَان وَبِدُونِ شَهَادَة.
npc.en: Yes, you can attend as a guest, but without an exam and without a certificate.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة، أَنَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ فَقَطْ. وَهَلْ أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى إِذْن مِنَ الدُّكْتُورَة؟
choices.en: No problem, I just want to learn. And do I need permission from the professor?
choices.feedback: Good: أَتَعَلَّمَ ends in -a after أَنْ, and أَحْتَاجُ goes with إِلَى: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى إِذْن.

choices.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة، أَنَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمُ فَقَطْ.
choices.en: No problem, I just want to learn. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَتَعَلَّمَ.

npc.ar: نَعَم. الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى غَائِبَة الْيَوْم، لٰكِنَّهَا عَائِدَة غَدًا. هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ لَهَا رِسَالَة؟
npc.en: Yes. Dr Mona is away today, but she's coming back tomorrow. Would you like to leave her a message?

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. قُولِي لَهَا إِنَّ فَيْصَلَ الْأَمْرِيكِيَّ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَحْضُرَ مُحَاضَرَاتِهَا.
choices.en: Yes, please. Tell her that Faisal, the American, would like to attend her lectures.
choices.feedback: Good: قُولِي is 'tell!' to a woman, and إِنَّ follows a verb of saying.

choices.ar: لَا، شُكْرًا. سَأَكْتُبُ لَهَا رِسَالَة رَسْمِيَّة الْيَوْم. مَا عُنْوَانُ بَرِيدِهَا الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيّ؟
choices.en: No, thank you. I'll write her a formal email today. What is her email address?
choices.feedback: Good: a polite 'no, thank you' and a plan of your own; رَسْمِيَّة agrees with رِسَالَة.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكِ. قُلْ لَهَا إِنَّ فَيْصَلَ الْأَمْرِيكِيَّ يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَحْضُرَ مُحَاضَرَاتِهَا.
choices.en: Yes, please. Tell her (to a man) that Faisal, the American, would like to attend her lectures.
choices.feedback: قُلْ is said to a man. The office worker is a woman: قُولِي لَهَا.

npc.ar: حَاضِر. وَمَا رَقْمُ هَاتِفِكَ؟ أَوْ يُمْكِنُكَ أَنْ تُرْسِلَ لَهَا رِسَالَة بِالْبَرِيدِ الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيّ.
npc.en: Certainly. And what's your phone number? Or you can send her an email.
segs: by the post, by the mail

choices.ar: سَأَكْتُبُ لَهَا رِسَالَة رَسْمِيَّة الْيَوْم. مَا عُنْوَانُ بَرِيدِهَا الْإِلِكْتُرُونِيّ؟
choices.en: I'll write her a formal email today. What is her email address?
choices.feedback: Good: you choose the email and ask for her address with مَا.

choices.ar: سَأَكْتُبُ لَهَا رِسَالَة رَسْمِيّ الْيَوْم.
choices.en: I'll write her a formal email today. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: رِسَالَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: رِسَالَة رَسْمِيَّة.

npc.ar: الْعُنْوَان عَلَى صَفْحَةِ الْكُلِّيَّة. وَلَا تَنْسَ: اُكْتُبْ حَضْرَةَ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى الْمُحْتَرَمَة.
npc.en: The address is on the faculty's web page. And don't forget: write 'Dear Dr Mona', with al-muḥtarama.
segs: (title of respect, lit. the presence of)

choices.ar: طَبْعًا! تَعَلَّمْتُ ذٰلِكَ فِي الْعَمَل. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Of course! I learnt that at work. Thank you very much, goodbye.
choices.feedback: Good: a formal call ends with شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا and مَعَ السَّلَامَة.

choices.ar: طَبْعًا! حَضْرَةَ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى الْمُحْتَرَم. شُكْرًا، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
choices.en: Of course! 'Dear Dr Mona', with al-muḥtaram. Thanks, goodbye. (wrong ending)
segs: (title of respect, lit. the presence of)
choices.feedback: Dr Mona is a woman, so the title takes ة: حَضْرَةَ الدُّكْتُورَة مُنَى الْمُحْتَرَمَة.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا فَيْصَل! عِيد مُبَارَك!
npc.en: Hello, Faisal! Happy Eid!

choices.ar: كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتِ بِخَيْر يَا سَيِّدَة سَمِيرَة! هٰذَا كَعْك لَكِ وَلِلْعَائِلَة.
choices.en: Many happy returns, Mrs Samira! This kaʿk is for you and the family.
choices.feedback: Good: كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتِ بِخَيْر with -ti for a woman, and a box of kaʿk as the Eid present.

choices.ar: كُلُّ عَامٍ وَأَنْتَ بِخَيْر يَا سَيِّدَة سَمِيرَة! هٰذَا كَعْك لَكِ وَلِلْعَائِلَة.
choices.en: Many happy returns (to a man), Mrs Samira! This kaʿk is for you and the family.
choices.feedback: Mrs Samira is a woman: وَأَنْتِ (wa-anti), not وَأَنْتَ.

npc.ar: وَأَنْتَ بِخَيْر يَا فَيْصَل! مَا أَلْطَفَكَ! تَفَضَّلْ، اُدْخُلْ، الْبَيْتُ بَيْتُكَ.
npc.en: And to you, Faisal! How kind of you! Please come in, make yourself at home.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. لَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُزْعِجَكُمْ فِي يَوْمِ الْعِيد.
choices.en: Thank you very much. I don't want to disturb you on Eid.
choices.feedback: Good: a polite guest says he does not want to disturb, and after أَنْ the verb takes -a before the suffix: أُزْعِجَكُمْ.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. لَا أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُزْعِجُكُمْ فِي يَوْمِ الْعِيد.
choices.en: Thank you very much. I don't want to disturb you on Eid. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in -a, also before a suffix: أَنْ أُزْعِجَكُمْ.

npc.ar: أَبَدًا! أَنْتَ جَارُنَا، وَالْجَارُ قَبْلَ الدَّار. اِجْلِسْ هُنَا، سَأُحْضِرُ لَكَ الشَّايَ.
npc.en: Not at all! You're our neighbour, and the neighbour comes before the house. Sit here, I'll bring you some tea.

choices.ar: بَيْتُكِ جَمِيل جِدًّا. وَمَنِ الْأَطْفَالُ الَّذِينَ فِي الشُّرْفَة؟
choices.en: Your home is very beautiful. And who are the children on the balcony?
segs: and who (-i links to the next word)
choices.feedback: Good: بَيْتُكِ with -ki for Mrs Samira, and الَّذِينَ for a group of people.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. وَمَاذَا تَفْعَلُونَ فِي الْعِيد عَادَةً؟
choices.en: Thank you. And what do you usually do at Eid?
choices.feedback: Good: تَفْعَلُونَ (you all) asks about the whole family, and عَادَةً carries -an as an adverb.

choices.ar: بَيْتُكِ جَمِيل جِدًّا. وَمَنِ الْأَطْفَالُ الَّذِي فِي الشُّرْفَة؟
choices.en: Your home is very beautiful. And who are the children on the balcony? (wrong form)
segs: and who (-i links to the next word)
who, which (m, one person or thing)
choices.feedback: For a group of people use الَّذِينَ, not الَّذِي: الْأَطْفَالُ الَّذِينَ فِي الشُّرْفَة.

npc.ar: هُمْ أَحْفَادِي. جَاؤُوا مِنَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّة أَمْسِ، وَأَخَذُوا عِيدِيَّة كَبِيرَة مِنْ جَدِّهِمْ!
npc.en: They're my grandchildren. They came from Alexandria yesterday, and they got a lot of Eid money from their grandfather!

choices.ar: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه! وَمَاذَا تَفْعَلُونَ فِي الْعِيد عَادَةً؟
choices.en: How wonderful! And what do you usually do at Eid?
choices.feedback: Good: مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه is what you say about children and good news.

choices.ar: آسِف جِدًّا!
choices.en: I'm very sorry!
choices.feedback: آسِف is for bad news or an apology. For grandchildren and a happy Eid say مَا شَاءَ اللّٰه!

npc.ar: نَزُورُ الْأَقَارِب، وَنَأْكُلُ كَثِيرًا، وَفِي الْمَسَاء نَخْرُجُ إِلَى الْحَدِيقَة أَوْ نَمْشِي عَلَى النِّيل.
npc.en: We visit relatives, we eat a lot, and in the evening we go out to the park or walk along the Nile.

choices.ar: وَهٰذَا الْكَعْك لَذِيذ جِدًّا! هَلْ صَنَعْتِهِ بِنَفْسِكِ؟
choices.en: And this kaʿk is very delicious! Did you make it yourself?
choices.feedback: Good: صَنَعْتِهِ بِنَفْسِكِ, 'you made it yourself', with -ti and -ki for a woman.

choices.ar: وَهٰذَا الْكَعْك لَذِيذ جِدًّا! هَلْ صَنَعْتَهُ بِنَفْسِكَ؟
choices.en: And this kaʿk is very delicious! Did you make it yourself? (to a man)
choices.feedback: صَنَعْتَهُ بِنَفْسِكَ is said to a man. To Mrs Samira: صَنَعْتِهِ بِنَفْسِكِ.

npc.ar: نَعَم، أَصْنَعُهُ كُلَّ سَنَة مَعَ بَنَاتِي. خُذْ مَعَكَ عُلْبَة لِأَصْدِقَائِكَ!
npc.en: Yes, I make it every year with my daughters. Take a box with you for your friends!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا سَيِّدَة سَمِيرَة. أَنْتِ جَارَة طَيِّبَة جِدًّا. عِيد مُبَارَك!
choices.en: Thank you, Mrs Samira. You're a very kind neighbour. Happy Eid!
choices.feedback: Good: جَارَة طَيِّبَة, both words with ة for a woman, and عِيد مُبَارَك is a warm goodbye.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا يَا سَيِّدَة سَمِيرَة. أَنْتِ جَارَة طَيِّب جِدًّا. عِيد مُبَارَك!
choices.en: Thank you, Mrs Samira. You're a very kind neighbour. Happy Eid! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: The adjective agrees with جَارَة, which is feminine: جَارَة طَيِّبَة, with ة.

npc.ar: مَسَاءُ الْخَيْر! أَيَّ فِيلْم تُرِيدُ أَنْ تُشَاهِدَ؟
npc.en: Good evening! Which film do you want to see?

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ تَذْكِرَتَيْنِ لِلْفِيلْمِ الْمِصْرِيِّ الْجَدِيدِ، الْفِيلْمِ الَّذِي يَتَكَلَّمُ عَنْهُ كُلُّ النَّاس.
choices.en: Good evening. I'd like two tickets for the new Egyptian film, the one that everybody is talking about.
choices.feedback: Good: as the object of أُرِيدُ, the dual ends in -ayni: تَذْكِرَتَيْنِ.

choices.ar: مَسَاءُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ تَذْكِرَتَانِ لِلْفِيلْمِ الْمِصْرِيِّ الْجَدِيدِ.
choices.en: Good evening. I'd like two tickets for the new Egyptian film. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: As the object of a verb the dual ends in -ayni: أُرِيدُ تَذْكِرَتَيْنِ, not تَذْكِرَتَانِ.

npc.ar: آهْ، الْفِيلْمُ الْمُضْحِك! هُنَاكَ عَرْض فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَة وَعَرْض فِي السَّاعَةِ الْعَاشِرَة.
npc.en: Ah, the comedy! There's a showing at seven o'clock and a showing at ten o'clock.

choices.ar: السَّابِعَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. صَدِيقِي قَالَ إِنَّ الْعَرْضَ الْأَخِيرَ يَنْتَهِي مُتَأَخِّرًا جِدًّا.
choices.en: Seven, please. My friend said that the last showing finishes very late.
choices.feedback: Good: after قَالَ comes إِنَّ, and its noun الْعَرْضَ takes -a.

choices.ar: السَّابِعَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. وَنُرِيدُ أَنْ نَجْلِسَ فِي الْوَسَط.
choices.en: Seven, please. And we'd like to sit in the middle.
choices.feedback: Good: نُرِيدُ أَنْ نَجْلِسَ speaks for you and Sami, and the verb after أَنْ ends in -a.

choices.ar: السَّابِعَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. صَدِيقِي قَالَ أَنَّ الْعَرْضَ الْأَخِيرَ يَنْتَهِي مُتَأَخِّرًا جِدًّا.
choices.en: Seven, please. My friend said that the last showing finishes very late. (wrong word)
choices.feedback: After قَالَ use إِنَّ, not أَنَّ: صَدِيقِي قَالَ إِنَّ الْعَرْضَ الْأَخِيرَ…

npc.ar: صَحِيح. أَيْنَ تُرِيدَانِ أَنْ تَجْلِسَا؟ فِي الْأَمَامِ أَمْ فِي الْوَسَط؟
npc.en: That's right. Where would you two like to sit? At the front or in the middle?

choices.ar: فِي الْوَسَط، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. فِي رَأْيِي، هٰذَا أَحْسَنُ مَكَان لِلشَّاشَة.
choices.en: In the middle, please. In my opinion, that's the best place for the screen.
choices.feedback: Good: he asks 'this or that?' (أَمْ), and you choose one and say why.

choices.ar: نَعَم، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ.
choices.en: Yes, please.
choices.feedback: He asks 'front or middle?' (أَمْ), so 'yes' does not answer. Choose one: فِي الْوَسَط.

npc.ar: عِنْدِي مَقْعَدَانِ فِي الصَّفِّ السَّابِع: رَقْمُ عَشَرَة وَرَقْمُ أَحَدَ عَشَرَ.
npc.en: I have two seats in row seven: number ten and number eleven.

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. بِكَمِ التَّذْكِرَة؟ وَهَلْ هُنَاكَ خَصْم لِلطُّلَّاب؟
choices.en: Excellent. How much is a ticket? And is there a discount for students?
segs: how much (-i links to the next word)
choices.feedback: Good: before al- the sukūn of كَمْ becomes i: بِكَمِ التَّذْكِرَة؟

choices.ar: مُمْتَاز. مَتَى التَّذْكِرَة؟
choices.en: Excellent. When is the ticket?
choices.feedback: مَتَى asks 'when'. To ask the price say بِكَمِ التَّذْكِرَة؟

npc.ar: التَّذْكِرَة بِمِئَة جُنَيْه، وَبِثَمَانِينَ لِلطُّلَّاب. هَلْ مَعَكَ بِطَاقَةُ الطَّالِب؟
npc.en: A ticket is a hundred pounds, and eighty for students. Do you have your student card?

choices.ar: نَعَم، تَفَضَّلْ. وَصَدِيقِي طَالِب أَيْضًا، لٰكِنَّهُ نَسِيَ بِطَاقَتَهُ فِي الْبَيْت.
choices.en: Yes, here you are. And my friend is a student too, but he forgot his card at home.
choices.feedback: Good: تَفَضَّلْ (to a man) as you hand over the card, and لٰكِنَّهُ ('but he') for your friend.

choices.ar: نَعَم، تَفَضَّلِي.
choices.en: Yes, here you are (to a woman).
choices.feedback: تَفَضَّلِي is for a woman. The ticket seller is a man: تَفَضَّلْ.

npc.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة هٰذِهِ الْمَرَّة. الْمَجْمُوعُ مِئَة وَسِتُّونَ جُنَيْهًا. وَالْفُشَار عَلَى الْيَمِين!
npc.en: No problem this time. That's a hundred and sixty pounds altogether. And the popcorn is on the right!

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! سَامِي سَيَكُونُ سَعِيدًا: الْفِيلْم وَالْفُشَار مَعًا!
choices.en: Thank you very much! Sami will be happy: the film and popcorn together!
choices.feedback: Good: after سَيَكُونُ the adjective takes -an: سَعِيدًا.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! سَامِي سَيَكُونُ سَعِيدَةً!
choices.en: Thank you very much! Sami will be happy! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: Sami is a man, so the adjective has no ة: سَامِي سَيَكُونُ سَعِيدًا.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر، أَهْلًا بِكَ فِي بَنْكِنَا! كَيْفَ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ الْيَوْمَ؟
npc.en: Good morning, welcome to our bank! How can I help you today?
segs: I help you (to a man, after an)

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أَنَا أَمْرِيكِيّ وَأَسْكُنُ فِي عَمَّان الْآنَ، وَأُرِيدُ أَنْ أَفْتَحَ حِسَابًا فِي بَنْكِكُمْ.
choices.en: Good morning. I'm American and I live in Amman now, and I'd like to open an account at your bank.
choices.feedback: Good: after أَنْ the verb ends in -a (أَفْتَحَ), and حِسَابًا is its object, with -an.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَفْتَحُ حِسَابًا فِي بَنْكِكُمْ.
choices.en: Good morning. I'd like to open an account at your bank. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: After أَنْ the verb takes the -a ending: أَنْ أَفْتَحَ, not أَفْتَحُ.

npc.ar: بِكُلِّ سُرُور. هَلْ مَعَكَ جَوَازُ سَفَرِكَ وَبِطَاقَةُ الْإِقَامَةِ وَإِثْبَاتُ الْعُنْوَان؟
npc.en: With pleasure. Do you have your passport, the residence card and proof of address with you?

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي وَهٰذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ الْإِقَامَة. لٰكِنْ لِلْأَسَف نَسِيتُ عَقْدَ الْإِيجَارِ فِي الْبَيْت!
choices.en: Here you are, this is my passport and this is the residence card. But unfortunately I forgot the rental contract at home!
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذَا for جَوَاز (m), هٰذِهِ for بِطَاقَة (f), and you say honestly what is missing.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، هٰذَا جَوَازُ سَفَرِي وَهٰذَا بِطَاقَةُ الْإِقَامَة.
choices.en: Here you are, this is my passport and this is the residence card. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: بِطَاقَة is feminine, so 'this' is هٰذِهِ: وَهٰذِهِ بِطَاقَةُ الْإِقَامَة.

npc.ar: لَا تَقْلَقْ. هَلْ عِنْدَكَ صُورَةُ الْعَقْدِ عَلَى هَاتِفِكَ؟ نَقْبَلُهَا الْيَوْمَ، وَتُحْضِرُ الْأَصْلَ غَدًا.
npc.en: Don't worry. Do you have a photo of the contract on your phone? We'll accept it today, and you bring the original tomorrow.

choices.ar: نَعَم، صَاحِبُ الشَّقَّةِ أَرْسَلَهُ لِي فِي رِسَالَة. انْظُرْ، هٰذَا هُوَ الْعَقْد.
choices.en: Yes, the owner of the flat sent it to me in a message. Look, this is the contract.
choices.feedback: Good: انْظُرْ is 'look!' to a man, and the owner of your flat (صَاحِبُ الشَّقَّةِ) sent the contract.

choices.ar: نَعَم، صَاحِبُ الشَّقَّةِ أَرْسَلَهُ لِي فِي رِسَالَة. انْظُرِي، هٰذَا هُوَ الْعَقْد.
choices.en: Yes, the owner of the flat sent it to me in a message. Look (to a woman), this is the contract.
choices.feedback: انْظُرِي is for a woman. The bank employee is a man: انْظُرْ.

npc.ar: مُمْتَاز، الصُّورَةُ وَاضِحَة. سَأَفْتَحُ لَكَ حِسَابًا جَارِيًا بِالدِّينَارِ الْأُرْدُنِّيِّ بِدُونِ رُسُوم شَهْرِيَّة.
npc.en: Excellent, the photo is clear. I'll open a current account in Jordanian dinars for you, with no monthly fees.

choices.ar: رَائِع! وَمَتَى أَحْصُلُ عَلَى بِطَاقَةِ الْبَنْك؟ أَحْتَاجُهَا لِلدَّفْعِ فِي الْمَحَلَّات.
choices.en: Great! And when do I get the bank card? I need it for paying in the shops.
choices.feedback: Good: أَحْصُلُ needs عَلَى: أَحْصُلُ عَلَى بِطَاقَةِ الْبَنْك.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي سُؤَال آخَر: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَصْرِفَ خَمْسَمِئَةِ دُولَار أَمْرِيكِيّ إِلَى دَنَانِيرَ. مَا سِعْرُ الصَّرْفِ الْيَوْمَ؟
choices.en: Thanks. I have another question: I'd like to change five hundred US dollars into dinars. What's the exchange rate today?
choices.feedback: Good: أَنْ أَصْرِفَ with -a, and after خَمْسَمِئَةِ the noun stays singular: دُولَار.

choices.ar: رَائِع! وَمَتَى أَحْصُلُ بِطَاقَةَ الْبَنْك؟
choices.en: Great! And when do I get the bank card? (missing word)
choices.feedback: This verb needs عَلَى before its object: مَتَى أَحْصُلُ عَلَى بِطَاقَةِ الْبَنْك؟

npc.ar: تَصِلُ الْبِطَاقَةُ بَعْدَ أُسْبُوع، وَسَنُرْسِلُ لَكَ رِسَالَةً عِنْدَمَا تَكُونُ جَاهِزَة.
npc.en: The card arrives in a week, and we'll send you a message when it's ready.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. عِنْدِي سُؤَال آخَر: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَصْرِفَ خَمْسَمِئَةِ دُولَار أَمْرِيكِيّ إِلَى دَنَانِيرَ. مَا سِعْرُ الصَّرْفِ الْيَوْمَ؟
choices.en: Thanks. I have another question: I'd like to change five hundred US dollars into dinars. What's the exchange rate today?
choices.feedback: Good: سُؤَال آخَر (both masculine), and after خَمْسَمِئَةِ the noun stays singular: دُولَار.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا. أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَصْرِفَ خَمْسَمِئَةِ دُولَارَات إِلَى دَنَانِيرَ.
choices.en: Thanks. I'd like to change five hundred dollars into dinars. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: After مِئَة (hundred) the counted noun is singular: خَمْسَمِئَةِ دُولَار, not دُولَارَات.

npc.ar: سِعْرُ الدِّينَارِ ثَابِتٌ مُقَابِلَ الدُّولَار: كُلُّ دُولَار بِحَوَالَيْ سَبْعِينَ قِرْشًا. سَتَحْصُلُ عَلَى حَوَالَيْ ثَلَاثِمِئَةٍ وَخَمْسِينَ دِينَارًا.
npc.en: The dinar has a fixed rate against the dollar: each dollar is about seventy piasters. You'll get about three hundred and fifty dinars.

choices.ar: هٰذَا جَيِّد. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! سَأُحْضِرُ عَقْدَ الْإِيجَارِ الْأَصْلِيَّ غَدًا صَبَاحًا، إِنْ شَاءَ اللّٰه.
choices.en: That's good. Thank you very much! I'll bring the original rental contract tomorrow morning, God willing.
choices.feedback: Good: you remember the original contract you left at home, and عَقْدَ takes -a as the object of سَأُحْضِرُ.

choices.ar: هٰذَا جَيِّدَة. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا!
choices.en: That's good. Thank you very much! (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هٰذَا is masculine, so the adjective has no ة: هٰذَا جَيِّد.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا يَا أَخِي، تَفَضَّلْ!
npc.en: Hello, my brother, go ahead!

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، سَاعِدْنِي مِنْ فَضْلِكَ! فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي، وَلَا أَعْرِفُ أَيْنَ هُوَ.
choices.en: Excuse me, help me please! I've lost my phone, and I don't know where it is.
choices.feedback: Good: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ and سَاعِدْنِي are the forms for a man, and فَقَدْتُ (-tu) is 'I lost'.

choices.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ، سَاعِدْنِي مِنْ فَضْلِكَ! فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفَكَ.
choices.en: Excuse me, help me please! I've lost your phone. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: هَاتِفَكَ means 'your phone'. Your own phone is هَاتِفِي: فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي.

npc.ar: لَا تَقْلَقْ يَا أَخِي. مَتَى رَأَيْتَهُ آخِرَ مَرَّة؟ هَلْ بَحَثْتَ فِي جُيُوبِكَ وَفِي حَقِيبَتِكَ؟
npc.en: Don't worry, my brother. When did you last see it? Did you look in your pockets and in your bag?

choices.ar: نَعَم، بَحَثْتُ فِي كُلِّ مَكَان. كَانَ فِي جَيْبِي قَبْلَ نِصْفِ سَاعَة، عِنْدَمَا اشْتَرَيْتُ الْقَهْوَة. وَمِحْفَظَتِي؟ لَا، هَا هِيَ فِي حَقِيبَتِي!
choices.en: Yes, I've looked everywhere. It was in my pocket half an hour ago, when I bought the coffee. And my wallet? No, here it is in my bag!
choices.feedback: Good: بَحَثْتُ with -tu is 'I looked', and كَانَ فِي جَيْبِي says where it was.

choices.ar: نَعَم، بَحَثْتَ فِي كُلِّ مَكَان.
choices.en: Yes, you looked everywhere. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: بَحَثْتَ (-ta) means 'you looked'. For 'I looked' say بَحَثْتُ (-tu).

npc.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه عَلَى الْمِحْفَظَة. السُّوق مُزْدَحِم الْيَوْمَ، فَمِنَ الْأَفْضَلِ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ إِلَى الشُّرْطَة السِّيَاحِيَّة. نُقْطَتُهُمْ قَرِيبَة جِدًّا مِنْ هُنَا.
npc.en: Thank God for the wallet. The market is crowded today, so it's better to go to the tourist police. Their police point is very close to here.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الشُّرْطَة السِّيَاحِيَّة الْآنَ.
choices.en: Thank you very much! I'll go to the tourist police now.
choices.feedback: Good: سَ + the present verb makes the future, سَأَذْهَبُ 'I will go', and السِّيَاحِيَّة agrees with الشُّرْطَة.

choices.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا! سَأَذْهَبُ إِلَى الشُّرْطَة السِّيَاحِيّ الْآنَ.
choices.en: Thank you very much! I'll go to the tourist police now. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: الشُّرْطَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: الشُّرْطَة السِّيَاحِيَّة.

npc.ar: أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا، تَفَضَّلِ اجْلِسْ. أَنَا هُنَا لِمُسَاعَدَتِكَ. مَاذَا حَدَثَ بِالضَّبْط؟
npc.en: Welcome, please sit down. I'm here to help you. What exactly happened?
segs: please (go ahead, to a man; -i links to the next word)
to help you (lit. for your help)

choices.ar: فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي فِي السُّوق قَبْلَ سَاعَة تَقْرِيبًا، قُرْبَ مَحَلِّ الْبَهَارَات. أَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ وَقَعَ مِنْ جَيْبِي.
choices.en: I lost my phone in the market about an hour ago, near the spice shop. I think it fell out of my pocket.
choices.feedback: Good: you say when and where, and أَنَّهُ follows أَظُنُّ ('I think that it').

choices.ar: فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي فِي السُّوق. هُوَ هَاتِف أَسْوَد كَبِير، وَلَهُ غِلَاف أَحْمَر عَلَيْهِ صُورَةُ جَمَل.
choices.en: I lost my phone in the market. It's a big black phone, and it has a red case with a picture of a camel on it.
choices.feedback: Good: غِلَاف is masculine, so the colour is أَحْمَر, and a clear description helps the police at once.

choices.ar: فَقَدَ هَاتِفِي فِي السُّوق قَبْلَ سَاعَة تَقْرِيبًا.
choices.en: He lost my phone in the market about an hour ago. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فَقَدَ means 'he lost'. For 'I lost' add -tu: فَقَدْتُ هَاتِفِي.

npc.ar: حَسَنًا، سَأَكْتُبُ تَقْرِيرًا الْآنَ. أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى اسْمِكَ وَعُنْوَانِكَ فِي عَمَّان.
npc.en: All right, I'll write a report now. I need your name and your address in Amman.

choices.ar: اسْمِي فَيْصَل، وَأَنَا أَمْرِيكِيّ مِنْ شِيكَاغُو. أَسْكُنُ فِي شَارِعِ الْقَلْعَة فِي جَبَلِ عَمَّان.
choices.en: My name is Faisal, and I'm American, from Chicago. I live on Citadel Street in Jabal Amman.
choices.feedback: Good: you give your name and the address of your flat; أَسْكُنُ فِي is 'I live in'.

choices.ar: اسْمِي فَيْصَل، وَأَنَا أَمْرِيكِيَّة مِنْ شِيكَاغُو.
choices.en: My name is Faisal, and I'm American, from Chicago. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: أَمْرِيكِيَّة is for a woman. Faisal says أَنَا أَمْرِيكِيّ.

npc.ar: لَحْظَة، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. زَمِيلِي يَقُولُ إِنَّ رَجُلًا أَحْضَرَ هَاتِفًا أَسْوَدَ بِغِلَاف أَحْمَر قَبْلَ عَشْرِ دَقَائِق! هَلْ هٰذَا هَاتِفُكَ؟
npc.en: One moment, please. My colleague says that a man brought in a black phone with a red case ten minutes ago! Is this your phone?

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا هُوَ، وَعَلَيْهِ الْجَمَل! الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه، شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا لَكَ وَلِلرَّجُلِ الطَّيِّب.
choices.en: Yes, that's it, with the camel on it! Thank God, thank you very much, to you and to the kind man.
choices.feedback: Good: هٰذَا هُوَ ('that's it') points to the phone, and لَكَ thanks the officer, a man.

choices.ar: نَعَم، هٰذَا هُوَ! شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا لَكِ.
choices.en: Yes, that's it! Thank you very much (to a woman).
choices.feedback: لَكِ is for a woman. The officer is a man: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا لَكَ.

npc.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر، أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا بِكَ فِي الْمَتْحَفِ الْأُرْدُنِّيّ! كَيْفَ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُسَاعِدَكَ؟
npc.en: Good morning, and welcome to the Jordan Museum! How can I help you?
segs: I can (lit. it is possible for me)
I help you (to a man, after an)

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. هٰذِهِ أَوَّلُ زِيَارَة لِي هُنَا. مَتَى يُغْلِقُ الْمَتْحَفُ الْيَوْمَ، وَبِكَمِ التَّذْكِرَة؟
choices.en: Good morning. This is my first visit here. When does the museum close today, and how much is a ticket?
segs: and how much (-i links to the next word)
choices.feedback: Good: مَتَى asks 'when', and بِكَمِ asks the price.

choices.ar: صَبَاحُ النُّور. أَيْنَ يُغْلِقُ الْمَتْحَفُ الْيَوْمَ؟
choices.en: Good morning. Where does the museum close today?
choices.feedback: أَيْنَ asks 'where'. For a time ask مَتَى: مَتَى يُغْلِقُ الْمَتْحَفُ الْيَوْمَ؟

npc.ar: الْمَتْحَفُ مَفْتُوح الْيَوْمَ حَتَّى السَّاعَةِ الْخَامِسَة. التَّذْكِرَةُ لِلْأَجَانِب بِخَمْسَةِ دَنَانِير، وَهِيَ أَرْخَصُ لِلْأُرْدُنِّيِّين.
npc.en: The museum is open today until five o'clock. A ticket for foreigners is five dinars, and it's cheaper for Jordanians.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مَعْقُول. هَلْ هُنَاكَ جَوْلَة مَعَ مُرْشِد؟ أُفَضِّلُ جَوْلَة بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة، لِأَنَّ عَرَبِيَّتِي مَا زَالَتْ ضَعِيفَة.
choices.en: That's reasonable. Is there a tour with a guide? I'd prefer a tour in English, because my Arabic is still weak.
choices.feedback: Good: عَرَبِيَّتِي is feminine, so ضَعِيفَة takes ة; مَا زَالَتْ means 'is still'.

choices.ar: هٰذَا مَعْقُول. أُفَضِّلُ جَوْلَة بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة، لِأَنَّ عَرَبِيَّتِي مَا زَالَتْ ضَعِيف.
choices.en: That's reasonable. I'd prefer a tour in English, because my Arabic is still weak. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: عَرَبِيَّتِي is feminine, so the adjective is ضَعِيفَة: عَرَبِيَّتِي مَا زَالَتْ ضَعِيفَة.

npc.ar: نَعَم، هُنَاكَ جَوْلَتَانِ بَعْدَ رُبْعِ سَاعَة: وَاحِدَة بِالْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة وَوَاحِدَة بِالْعَرَبِيَّة. كُلُّ جَوْلَة بِدِينَارَيْنِ.
npc.en: Yes, there are two tours in a quarter of an hour: one in English and one in Arabic. Each tour costs two dinars.

choices.ar: طَيِّب. وَهَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُصَوِّرَ فِي الْقَاعَات؟ وَهَلْ عِنْدَكُمْ خَرِيطَة لِلْمَتْحَف؟
choices.en: Okay. And can I take photos in the halls? And do you have a map of the museum?
segs: I can (lit. it is possible for me)
you have (to a group; lit. at you)
choices.feedback: Good: after يُمْكِنُنِي come أَنْ and a verb ending in -a: أَنْ أُصَوِّرَ.

choices.ar: طَيِّب. وَهَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أُصَوِّرُ فِي الْقَاعَات؟
choices.en: Okay. And can I I take photos in the halls? (wrong form)
segs: I can (lit. it is possible for me)
choices.feedback: After يُمْكِنُنِي you need أَنْ and the -a ending: هَلْ يُمْكِنُنِي أَنْ أُصَوِّرَ؟

npc.ar: التَّصْوِيرُ مَسْمُوح، لٰكِنْ بِدُونِ فَلَاش. وَهٰذِهِ خَرِيطَة مَجَّانِيَّة. آهْ، لَحْظَة… لِلْأَسَف، الْجَوْلَةُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةُ مُمْتَلِئَة.
npc.en: Photography is allowed, but without flash. And here is a free map. Oh, one moment... unfortunately, the English tour is full.

choices.ar: مُمْتَلِئَة؟ يَا خَسَارَة! وَمَتَى الْجَوْلَةُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةُ التَّالِيَة؟
choices.en: Full? What a pity! And when is the next English tour?
choices.feedback: Good: مُمْتَلِئَة and التَّالِيَة take ة to agree with الْجَوْلَة.

choices.ar: يَا خَسَارَة! إِذًا سَأَنْضَمُّ إِلَى الْجَوْلَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّة.
choices.en: What a pity! Then I'll join the Arabic tour.
choices.feedback: Good: you switch to the Arabic tour, which is excellent practice. إِذًا means 'so, then'.

choices.ar: مُمْتَلِئ؟ يَا خَسَارَة! وَمَتَى الْجَوْلَةُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةُ التَّالِيَة؟
choices.en: Full? What a pity! And when is the next English tour? (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: You mean الْجَوْلَة, which is feminine: مُمْتَلِئَة؟

npc.ar: بَعْدَ الظُّهْر، فِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّالِثَة. لٰكِنْ فِي الْجَوْلَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ مَكَان، وَالْمُرْشِدُ يَتَكَلَّمُ بِبُطْء وَبِوُضُوح.
npc.en: In the afternoon, at three o'clock. But there is room on the Arabic tour, and the guide speaks slowly and clearly.

choices.ar: فِكْرَة جَيِّدَة! سَأَنْضَمُّ إِلَى الْجَوْلَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّة. هٰذَا تَمْرِين مُمْتَاز لِي بَعْدَ دُرُوسِ الْعَرَبِيَّة.
choices.en: Good idea! I'll join the Arabic tour. That's excellent practice for me after my Arabic lessons.
choices.feedback: Good: فِكْرَة is feminine, so جَيِّدَة; and you take the tour that has room.

choices.ar: فِكْرَة جَيِّد! سَأَنْضَمُّ إِلَى الْجَوْلَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّة.
choices.en: Good idea! I'll join the Arabic tour. (wrong ending)
choices.feedback: فِكْرَة is feminine, so the adjective takes ة: فِكْرَة جَيِّدَة.

npc.ar: تَذْكِرَة وَاحِدَة وَمَكَان فِي الْجَوْلَة: الْمَجْمُوعُ سَبْعَةُ دَنَانِير، خَمْسَة لِلتَّذْكِرَة وَاثْنَانِ لِلْجَوْلَة.
npc.en: One ticket and a place on the tour: that's seven dinars altogether, five for the ticket and two for the tour.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، سَبْعَةُ دَنَانِير. أَيْنَ تَبْدَأُ الْجَوْلَة؟ وَمَا اسْمُ الْمُرْشِد؟
choices.en: Here you are, seven dinars. Where does the tour start? And what is the guide's name?
choices.feedback: Good: after the numbers 3 to 10 the noun is plural: سَبْعَةُ دَنَانِير.

choices.ar: تَفَضَّلْ، سَبْعَة دِينَار.
choices.en: Here you are, seven dinar. (wrong form)
choices.feedback: After the numbers 3 to 10 the noun is plural: سَبْعَةُ دَنَانِير, not سَبْعَة دِينَار.
